not-built-for-me.name: Disability
not-built-for-me.line: Places and services aren't built for my disability.
not-built-for-me.why: "I can't access things I need" could be about money or distance; this says what the ID names, that the world isn't built for someone like me.

not-built-for-me.name: Access
not-built-for-me.line: Buildings, websites and services shut me out because of my disability.
not-built-for-me.why: Names concrete places people get shut out of, and gives an area-style label like the rest of the heading.

always-tired.name: Tired
always-tired.line: I'm worn out all day, even when I've slept.
always-tired.why: Separates daytime exhaustion from Sleep, so someone who sleeps fine but is still drained knows this one is theirs.

always-tired.name: Energy
always-tired.why: Keeps the plain line and makes the name an area like Sleep, Fitness and Diet, so the heading doesn't mix problems and areas.

health-runs-my-life.name: Health condition
health-runs-my-life.line: I'm living with a condition that limits me.
health-runs-my-life.why: Keeps the line and turns the label into an area, matching Sleep, Fitness, Healthcare and Diet.

health-runs-my-life.name: Illness
health-runs-my-life.line: A long-term illness shapes most of my days.
health-runs-my-life.why: Closer to what the ID names, health running my life, while staying plain and making clear it's ongoing, not a passing cold.

pairs.distinction: Sleep is about nights; Tired is about days, including people who sleep fine but are drained by illness, work or caregiving.
pairs.reason: Plenty of people are exhausted without a sleep problem, and the sharper Tired line above makes that choice obvious.

pairs.distinction: Pain is hurting most days, whatever the cause; Illness is a condition that limits you, often without pain.
pairs.reason: Daily pain is common enough and specific enough that people look for it by name, and many limiting conditions don't hurt.

pairs.distinction: Illness is living with a condition; Healthcare is not being able to see a doctor when you need one.
pairs.reason: One is about your body and the other about the system around it, and many people have one without the other.

pairs.distinction: Hormones is losing days to a monthly cycle or menopause, which most people wouldn't call a condition.
pairs.reason: Someone losing days to periods or menopause wouldn't look under a heading about living with an illness.

pairs.distinction: Senses is losing sight or hearing over time; Disability is the world not being built for you.
pairs.reason: Many people losing their sight or hearing don't think of themselves as disabled, and many disabled people's problem is access, not their senses.

pairs.distinction: Teeth is dental care, which is insured and paid for separately from seeing a doctor.
pairs.reason: People who can see a doctor often still can't afford a dentist, and they name it on its own.

pairs.distinction: Diet is what you eat; Fitness is how fit and active you feel.
pairs.reason: Someone can eat well and still feel out of shape, or the reverse, so the choice is easy.

pairs.distinction: Tired is physical tiredness from any cause; Burnout is being used up by work.
pairs.reason: Burnout sits under Work and names the cause, while Tired is for anyone worn out whatever the reason.

pairs.distinction: Healthcare is not being able to see a doctor; Medical bills is worrying about what care will cost.
pairs.reason: Getting seen and paying for it are different worries, and the societal page already frames cost as a shared problem.

pairs.distinction: Diet is not eating the way you want; running out of food is not having enough to eat.
pairs.reason: Not having enough food is a money problem and belongs under Money, while Diet is about the kind of food you eat.

pairs.distinction: Disability is places and services not built for you; Discrimination is people treating you worse because of who you are.
pairs.reason: A missing ramp and being treated worse by a person are different problems, and one sits on each page.

anxiety.name: Anxiety
anxiety.line: My mind keeps running through what could go wrong.
anxiety.why: Keeps the worry at the center but says what it looks like in a day, a mind that won't stop rehearsing the worst.

anxiety.name: Anxiety
anxiety.line: I worry so much that I can't settle, even when things are fine.
anxiety.why: Keeps the original 'I worry' and adds what makes it a pain: the worry stays when nothing is actually wrong.

overwhelmed.name: Stress
overwhelmed.line: There's so much on my plate that I can't catch up.
overwhelmed.why: Says what being overwhelmed looks like day to day, too many things at once, which also sets it apart from Anxiety's worry about what might happen.

overwhelmed.name: Overwhelmed
overwhelmed.line: I have so much going on that I can't think straight.
overwhelmed.why: Uses the word the ID names and the person's own feeling, and shows the effect: too much at once crowds out clear thinking.

hard-on-myself.name: Hard on myself
hard-on-myself.line: Whatever I do, I tell myself it isn't good enough.
hard-on-myself.why: Names the problem the way the ID does instead of the area Self-esteem, so the heading reads as problems like Anxiety and Grief, and shows the inner voice in action.

hard-on-myself.name: Hard on myself
hard-on-myself.line: I'm never good enough for myself.
hard-on-myself.why: Keeps the original line, which people recognize, and only turns the area name Self-esteem into a problem name like the rest of the heading.

cant-focus.name: Can't focus
cant-focus.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing for long.
cant-focus.why: Turns the area name Focus into a problem name like the rest of the heading and keeps the original line with a small clarifying ending.

short-fuse.name: Short fuse
short-fuse.line: I snap at people I love over small things.
short-fuse.why: Brings the name back to the short fuse the ID names, and adds 'over small things' so it reads as a quick temper, not general anger at something unfair.

feeling-down.name: Feeling down
feeling-down.line: I feel low most days, and nothing seems worth the effort.
feeling-down.why: Uses the everyday words the ID names instead of a diagnosis, and says what low days look like, so people who'd never call it depression still recognize it.

drinking-too-much.name: Addiction
drinking-too-much.line: I can't stop drinking, using or gambling, even though it hurts me.
drinking-too-much.why: Keeps the broad name but says plainly what it is, so people can recognize their own habit instead of guessing what 'something' means.

drinking-too-much.name: Drinking too much
drinking-too-much.line: I drink more than I want to and can't cut back.
drinking-too-much.why: Brings the wording back to the drinking the ID names, in the person's own words, at the cost of leaving other addictions to their own pains.

pairs.distinction: Anxiety is worry about what might go wrong; Stress is having too much going on right now.
pairs.reason: Someone with a calm schedule can still worry all day, and someone buried in tasks may not be worried at all, so people can tell which one they live with.

pairs.distinction: Stress is the feeling of too much at once from any source; Paperwork is the time lost to forms, bills and phone queues.
pairs.reason: Paperwork is one specific cause with its own fixes, while being overwhelmed can come from work, family or anything else.

pairs.distinction: Short fuse is my own temper with people I love; Family is being caught in fighting at home that others start too.
pairs.reason: One is about how I react and the other is about the home I live in, and a person knows whether the problem is mostly them or the household.

pairs.distinction: Short fuse is how I treat people when I'm on edge; Stress is the load that may put me there.
pairs.reason: Plenty of stressed people don't snap at anyone, and the fixes for a quick temper are different from the fixes for too much on my plate.

pairs.distinction: Feeling down is low mood and nothing seeming worth it; Anxiety is a mind racing with worry.
pairs.reason: They often come together, but people describe them very differently and would pick the one that sounds like their days.

pairs.distinction: Feeling down is low mood across life; Burnout is being worn out, usually by work.
pairs.reason: Burnout sits under Work because rest and changes at work help it, while feeling low most days reaches beyond work.

pairs.distinction: Hard on myself is the voice that says I'm never good enough; Feeling down is a low mood that may have no such voice.
pairs.reason: Many people who judge themselves harshly don't feel low most days, so they would choose without hesitating.

pairs.distinction: Trauma is living with one thing that happened; Feeling down is a general low mood with or without a cause.
pairs.reason: Someone shaped by a past event knows it is about that event, and it needs its own care and, later, its own crisis resources.

pairs.distinction: Trauma is about something that already happened; Anxiety is worry about what might happen.
pairs.reason: The past event is the center of one and absent from the other, so the person living it can tell them apart.

pairs.distinction: Can't focus is my attention drifting once I start; Procrastination is not starting at all.
pairs.reason: People know whether their trouble is getting going or staying with it, and the fixes differ.

pairs.distinction: Can't focus is attention that won't stay on any one thing; Doomscrolling is evenings lost to the phone.
pairs.reason: The phone is one cause of scattered attention, but plenty of people can't focus with the phone put away.

pairs.distinction: Grief is missing one person I lost; Loneliness is not having people around me now.
pairs.reason: A grieving person can be surrounded by family and still miss the one who died, so the two are easy to tell apart.

Main sources: SAMHSA NSDUH 2024 annual report, WHO mental disorders fact sheet (2026 update), Crisis Text Line United in Empathy 2023 issue shares, Gallup State of the World's Emotional Health 2026, Ipsos Health Service Report 2026, APA Stress in America 2025 (apa.org returned an empty page, so UPI's report of the findings is used), CDC MMWR on subjective cognitive decline. Gallup Most Important Problem names no mental-health item (only Drugs, under 1%); Ipsos What Worries the World has no mind item, so the Ipsos Health Service Report stands in. 211's snapshot names mental health and substance use as a top referral category without a count. oecd.org returned 403; OECD entries are the Subjective well-being indicators by name plus TUAC's passage on deaths of despair. Eurostat's quality-of-life page loaded but reports only life satisfaction, so it is not listed. Wikidata QIDs via wbsearchentities (rate-limited; about 30 lookups, not counted as searches). Six candidates, all with opened sources. suicidal-thoughts and self-harm should be tagged sensitive; serious-mental-illness and eating-and-body-image probably too. mental-health-care overlaps cant-get-care (Healthcare) and may belong under Body or societal Health; refine should decide. memory overlaps seeing-hearing (Senses) as an aging pain. Leads not proposed: gambling (mapped broader to drinking-too-much, whose line covers any compulsion), panic attacks and phobias (anxiety), ADHD (cant-focus), meaning in life (left to the Purpose sweep), bullying (out of scope; People, Kids or Safety).

proposed.name: Anxiety
proposed.line: My mind keeps running through what could go wrong.

alternatives.name: Anxiety
alternatives.line: I worry so much that I can't settle, even when things are fine.

why.detail: Keeps the worry at the center but says what it looks like in a day, a mind that won't stop rehearsing the worst.

current.name: Stress
current.line: I'm overwhelmed.

proposed.name: Stress
proposed.line: There's so much on my plate that I can't catch up.

alternatives.name: Overwhelmed
alternatives.line: I have so much going on that I can't think straight.

why.detail: Says what being overwhelmed looks like day to day, too many things at once, which also sets it apart from Anxiety's worry about what might happen.

current.name: Self-esteem
current.line: I'm never good enough for myself.

proposed.name: Hard on myself
proposed.line: Whatever I do, I tell myself it isn't good enough.

alternatives.name: Hard on myself
alternatives.line: I'm never good enough for myself.

why.detail: Names the problem the way the ID does instead of the area Self-esteem, so the heading reads as problems like Anxiety and Grief, and shows the inner voice in action.

current.name: Focus
current.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

proposed.name: Can't focus
proposed.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing for long.

why.detail: Turns the area name Focus into a problem name like the rest of the heading and keeps the original line with a small clarifying ending.

current.name: Anger
current.line: I snap at people I love.

proposed.name: Short fuse
proposed.line: I snap at people I love over small things.

why.detail: Brings the name back to the short fuse the ID names, and adds 'over small things' so it reads as a quick temper, not general anger at something unfair.

current.name: Depression
current.line: I feel low most days.

proposed.name: Feeling down
proposed.line: I feel low most days, and nothing seems worth the effort.

why.detail: Uses the everyday words the ID names instead of a diagnosis, and says what low days look like, so people who'd never call it depression still recognize it.

current.name: Addiction
current.line: I can't stop something that's hurting me.

proposed.name: Addiction
proposed.line: I can't stop drinking, using or gambling, even though it hurts me.

alternatives.name: Drinking too much
alternatives.line: I drink more than I want to and can't cut back.

why.detail: Keeps the broad name but says plainly what it is, so people can recognize their own habit instead of guessing what 'something' means.

side.name: Anxiety
side.line: I worry too much.

side.name: Stress
side.line: I'm overwhelmed.

why.detail: Someone with a calm schedule can still worry all day, and someone buried in tasks may not be worried at all, so people can tell which one they live with. Anxiety is worry about what might go wrong; Stress is having too much going on right now.

current.name: Anxiety
current.line: I worry too much.

proposed.name: Stress
proposed.line: I'm overwhelmed.

side.name: Stress
side.line: I'm overwhelmed.

side.name: Paperwork
side.line: I lose my week to forms, bills and phone queues.

why.detail: Paperwork is one specific cause with its own fixes, while being overwhelmed can come from work, family or anything else. Stress is the feeling of too much at once from any source; Paperwork is the time lost to forms, bills and phone queues.

current.name: Stress
current.line: I'm overwhelmed.

proposed.name: Paperwork
proposed.line: I lose my week to forms, bills and phone queues.

side.name: Anger
side.line: I snap at people I love.

side.name: Family
side.line: I'm caught in fighting at home.

why.detail: One is about how I react and the other is about the home I live in, and a person knows whether the problem is mostly them or the household. Short fuse is my own temper with people I love; Family is being caught in fighting at home that others start too.

current.name: Anger
current.line: I snap at people I love.

proposed.name: Family
proposed.line: I'm caught in fighting at home.

side.name: Anger
side.line: I snap at people I love.

side.name: Stress
side.line: I'm overwhelmed.

why.detail: Plenty of stressed people don't snap at anyone, and the fixes for a quick temper are different from the fixes for too much on my plate. Short fuse is how I treat people when I'm on edge; Stress is the load that may put me there.

current.name: Anger
current.line: I snap at people I love.

proposed.name: Stress
proposed.line: I'm overwhelmed.

side.name: Depression
side.line: I feel low most days.

side.name: Anxiety
side.line: I worry too much.

why.detail: They often come together, but people describe them very differently and would pick the one that sounds like their days. Feeling down is low mood and nothing seeming worth it; Anxiety is a mind racing with worry.

current.name: Depression
current.line: I feel low most days.

proposed.name: Anxiety
proposed.line: I worry too much.

side.name: Depression
side.line: I feel low most days.

side.name: Burnout
side.line: I've got nothing left.

why.detail: Burnout sits under Work because rest and changes at work help it, while feeling low most days reaches beyond work. Feeling down is low mood across life; Burnout is being worn out, usually by work.

current.name: Depression
current.line: I feel low most days.

proposed.name: Burnout
proposed.line: I've got nothing left.

side.name: Self-esteem
side.line: I'm never good enough for myself.

side.name: Depression
side.line: I feel low most days.

why.detail: Many people who judge themselves harshly don't feel low most days, so they would choose without hesitating. Hard on myself is the voice that says I'm never good enough; Feeling down is a low mood that may have no such voice.

current.name: Self-esteem
current.line: I'm never good enough for myself.

proposed.name: Depression
proposed.line: I feel low most days.

side.name: Trauma
side.line: I'm still living with something that happened.

side.name: Depression
side.line: I feel low most days.

why.detail: Someone shaped by a past event knows it is about that event, and it needs its own care and, later, its own crisis resources. Trauma is living with one thing that happened; Feeling down is a general low mood with or without a cause.

current.name: Trauma
current.line: I'm still living with something that happened.

proposed.name: Depression
proposed.line: I feel low most days.

side.name: Trauma
side.line: I'm still living with something that happened.

side.name: Anxiety
side.line: I worry too much.

why.detail: The past event is the center of one and absent from the other, so the person living it can tell them apart. Trauma is about something that already happened; Anxiety is worry about what might happen.

current.name: Trauma
current.line: I'm still living with something that happened.

proposed.name: Anxiety
proposed.line: I worry too much.

side.name: Focus
side.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

side.name: Procrastination
side.line: I put things off.

why.detail: People know whether their trouble is getting going or staying with it, and the fixes differ. Can't focus is my attention drifting once I start; Procrastination is not starting at all.

current.name: Focus
current.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

proposed.name: Procrastination
proposed.line: I put things off.

side.name: Focus
side.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

side.name: Doomscrolling
side.line: I lose my nights to my phone.

why.detail: The phone is one cause of scattered attention, but plenty of people can't focus with the phone put away. Can't focus is attention that won't stay on any one thing; Doomscrolling is evenings lost to the phone.

current.name: Focus
current.line: I can't keep my mind on one thing.

proposed.name: Doomscrolling
proposed.line: I lose my nights to my phone.

side.name: Grief
side.line: I'm missing someone I lost.

side.name: Loneliness
side.line: I feel alone.

why.detail: A grieving person can be surrounded by family and still miss the one who died, so the two are easy to tell apart. Grief is missing one person I lost; Loneliness is not having people around me now.

current.name: Grief
current.line: I'm missing someone I lost.

proposed.name: Loneliness
proposed.line: I feel alone.
